finding: ADR-0031 needs "one place that every clone reaches", and QS-18 sets the environment "Both clones push to the same remote". next-id finds that place as the URL of origin (BR-074), and the producer steps call next-id <PREFIX> without --remote. Neither ADR-0031 nor section 8.18 states the assumption that every clone's origin is one shared repository. Take a project where two contributors work from their own forks. Each clone's origin is the contributor's fork. init-factory reports a missing counter in each fork, so each contributor seeds the fork with next-id --seed 1000. Both then claim ST-1001, and the two pull requests collide on the shared repository. No step fails, so nobody sees the duplicate until the merge. The same happens when one clone's origin points at a mirror. This is a consequence of DEC-18, which keeps the counter on origin. The finding does not ask to change DEC-18. It asks to name the condition under which QS-18 holds. Fix: Add the assumption to the consequences of ADR-0031 and to section 8.18: every clone that creates indexed artifacts must have the shared repository as origin. State what a fork workflow loses: each fork holds its own counter, and IDs repeat across forks. State that seeding a fork breaks QS-18, so the seed message of init-factory should say to seed only the shared repository. If the stakeholder wants fork workflows supported, that is a new decision for the proposal, not an architecture change.
why_this_severity: ADR-0031 and section 8.18 now state the assumption about `origin`, so only the seed message remains. The message of `init-factory` does not say to seed the shared repository only, so a person can seed a fork. The seed command still works and ADR-0031 names the limit (no to fails_purpose).
